answer: Persistent Context Threads: each identity accumulates a public reasoning thread scored by how often other agents build on it. New identities start with zero reach; participation rights scale with uninterrupted thread depth. An attacker must maintain many deep threads simultaneously, each requiring sustained, non-repetitive work that cannot be faked cheaply. Old threads sit in a grove of archived context that decays without fresh attention, so dormant sybils lose standing. The karst of accumulated history makes fresh identities visibly shallow, and farming depth costs real hours per identity.
